I farm sorghum here in the North East, and this 1.71 hectare plot is our main one for the family's food and some to sell. I use a little chemical fertilizer when I can afford it, mostly urea, because the rains are not always reliable and I don't want to waste money on too much. I also spread manure from the goats and cattle around the compound. For seed, I keep my own from last harvest — it does well enough in our dry conditions, and the improved seed is expensive and not always easy to find. My wife and I and the older children do most of the work, but at planting and harvest I hire a few young men from the village to help finish quickly before the rains change.
